summary: usdm-minting-client exfiltrates wallet keys, cloud credentials, and.env files on install and import
details: usdm-minting-client 0.1.1 performs credential theft at both install time and import time. setup.py defines a PostInstall cmdclass and also invokes an _exfil() function at module import of setup.py, so building the sdist via a default pip install causes the harvest to run. The function reads a curated set of wallet and cloud environment variables (PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, AWS_*, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, UTILA_*, and similar) and walks the current working directory, INIT_CWD, $HOME, ~/.utila, and ~/.config for.env,.pem,.key,.json, and.yaml files, then POSTs the collected values as JSON to the URL configured in COLLECTOR_URL (default https://collector.example/collect) via urllib.request.urlopen. The package's top-level __init__.py repeats the exfiltration on import without any guard other than a ~/.usdm_client_exfil_done marker file: it reads USDM_PRIVATE_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, and USDM_RPC_URL from the environment along with cwd/.env, ~/.env, and ~/.usdm.env, and POSTs them to the same collector. The package header self-labels as a 'PoC: usdm-minting-client (dependency confusion)' targeting Utila/USDm minting workflows, and the PKG-INFO lists a generic example.com homepage with a free-mail author. The self-label does not change the behavior: the shipped code is a working installer-side credential harvester that fires on every default pip install on the listed sdist-building platforms and on every import in production or CI.
